name: MAW Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: MAW's top belt. Erik Strong holds it when the diary opens and defends it at nine of the first ten shows (Spring Fever's main event is a tag match), against Jean Cattley, Findlay O'Farraday, Citizen X, Ricky Douglas, Raphael, Antonio, Davis Wayne Newton and Jacob Jett, before losing it to Jean Cattley in a three-way with Black Eagle at Where It All Begins Again in October 2008. Jean Cattley keeps it against Erik Strong in a best-of-three-falls rematch at Remember November, then against Black Eagle, Ultimate Phoenix twice, Fumihiro Ota, the Masked Patriot, Stevie Grayson, Jacob Jett and Trent Shaffer, and fights Steven Parker to a time-limit draw at Iron in August 2009; the diary's own title records give the reign twelve defences. Cattley and Steven Parker draw again at Fall Of The King in September 2009; Parker then beats him for it in a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again in October 2009, keeps it against Darryl Devine and Cameron Vessey, and loses it at The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2010 to Jay Chord, who cashes in the title shot guaranteed to the previous year's Invitational winner; Jay keeps it against Thom Morgan, Stevie Grayson, Amazing Fire Fly and Kirk Jameson and fights Aaron Andrews to a time-limit draw at April Showers. The diary's own title records give Parker's second reign ten defences and Jay Chord's sixteen. Jay Chord keeps the belt through the summer of 2010 against Erik Strong, the Masked Patriot, Fumihiro Ota and Firebird in a three-way, Brandon Smith, Steve Flash and Trent Shaffer, until Aaron Andrews beats him in a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2010, by two falls to one, after Rip Chord's bell and a referee's reversal of the last fall; Andrews keeps the belt against Joey Poison (Toxin) at Eleventh Hour in November. The diary's own title records list Andrews's reign as "Aaron Andrews October 2010 41". Aaron Andrews keeps the belt against Hugh de Aske at Remember November, Matthew Gauge at Season's Beatings, Jay Chord in a street fight at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011 (the match the narrator calls MAW's best ever), Primus Allen at The Rip Chord Invitational, Firebird at March Madness and JD Morgan at April Showers; Tommy Cornell's threat to pull him back to TCW fails when he signs a new deal for a full year. In the diary's pages to September 2011 he keeps the belt against Black Eagle on 12th May, Erik Strong on 26th May, Kirk Jameson, Hugh de Aske, JD Morgan, Firebird and Jay Chord in a six-man Gold Rush match on 12th June, in which he turns on Jameson with a Standing Hot Shot onto an exposed turnbuckle, Fumihiro Ota on 12th July, Hugh de Aske on 26th July, Steve Flash on 12th August, Chance Fortune on 26th August and Ernest Youngman on 12th September. In the diary's pages to January 2012 he keeps the belt against Brandon Smith on 26th September, Randy Bumfhole in a time-limit draw on 12th October, Kirk Jameson, who cashes in the guaranteed shot of the Invitational title, on 26th October, Chance Fortune, Steve Flash and Fumihiro Ota, having written into a new contract the right to refuse challengers, and Randy Bumfhole again at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012. In the diary's pages from February to May 2012 he keeps the belt against Jared Johnson at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February, Kashmir Singh at All Or Nothing on 12th February, Wanda Fish on 2nd March, in her last match, Brandon Smith on 5th March and Jim Force on 12th March; at April Showers on 5th April, one of the six champions in the Gold Rush match, he gets Randy Bumfhole thrown out of the field by using his right to refuse a challenger and comes through without being pinned. He keeps it against Steve Gumble on 8th April, Randy Bumfhole in a steel cage match on 12th April, which the narrator counts as his thirtieth title defence, and Donnie J in a title-versus-title match on 5th May, which wins him the All Action belt as well, and again in a thirty-minute Iron Man match on 12th May, which he wins by two falls to one, by the skin of his teeth. In the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he keeps the belt against Lassana Makutsi at High Noon on 5th June, which he chooses to open the show, Fumihiro Ota at South East Madness on 9th June, in a thirty-minute match the narrator counts as his thirty-fourth defence, KC Glenn at Summer Showdown on 12th June, who cashes in a guaranteed title shot, Bradford Peverell at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, in what the narrator calls the worst main event in years, Kid Toma at Beach Blast on 12th July and Rich Money at Summernova on 5th August, in a thirty-minute draw. At Summer Showdown he swings the belt into Kirk Jameson's head and joins The Fallen, and at Back To School on 5th September he loses a non-title steel cage match to Money. He is still the champion in the diary's pages for September 2012.

name: MAW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: MAW's tag belts. The Canadian Blondes hold them when the diary opens, Perez & Shaffer win them in the Beach Blast ladder match in July 2008, and Trent Shaffer carries them into the autumn with a new partner, Stevie Grayson. The Gauge Brothers take the belts from Shaffer & Grayson at The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2009, Morgan & Benning take them at All Or Nothing in February and keep them against C-V-2 and the Canadian Blondes, and C-V-2 win them at Iron in August 2009. C-V-2 keep the belts against the Internet Favourites, the Masked Patriot and Kashmir Singh, Riley McManus and Shane Nelson, and Ultimate Phoenix and Kashmir Singh; Cameron Vessey leaves for USPW in March 2010, and Casey Valentine and Jared Johnson carry the belts on, keeping them in the April Showers three-way, against Morgan & Benning at Spring Fever and against Shaffer & Grayson at Mother, May I?. The diary's own title records list the whole reign as "Valentine & Johnson", with nine defences. Casey Valentine and Jared Johnson keep the belts against the Internet Favourites, Morgan & Benning and, in a three-way, the Internet Favourites and Ricochet & Sharp, until the Canadian Blondes beat them in a three-way at Fall Of The King in September 2010 for a record third reign; the Blondes keep them in a four-team ladder match at Where It All Begins Again in October and against Brandon Smith and Joe Benning on a November tour show. The diary's own title records list the Blondes' reign as "The Canadian Blondes (3) September 2010". The Canadian Blondes keep the belts against Smith & Singh at Remember November, the Internet Favourites on 11th December, the Bailey Boys at Season's Beatings and Smith & Singh on 25th December, until Kashmir Singh and Jean Cattley, a pair thrown together when the Blondes injure Brandon Smith, beat them at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011. Cattley and Singh keep the belts against Antonio & Raphael, the Blondes and Thrash and Firebird, until the Canadian Blondes beat them at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011 and Jean Cattley loses a Loser Leaves Town match to Casey Valentine and leaves for the SWF. The diary's own title records list the reign as "Cattley & Singh January 2011 3". The Blondes keep the belts against the Young Americans, Smith & Singh with the Dark Raptors, Kid Arachnid and Amazing Fire Fly, the West Texas Peacekeepers, Smith & Singh with Ford & Speed, Leftie Wilkes and Ben Williams, The Quest and the Young Americans again,, the Young Americans and Smith & Singh in a three-way on 26th September, the Young Americans again and the Internet Favourites, until Smith & Singh take the belts from them at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011, ending the fourth reign at six months. Smith & Singh keep them against the Second Sons, in a three-way with the Dark Raptors and Ford & Speed, against Ford & Speed, Firebird and Citizen X and, at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012, in a three-way with Ford & Speed and Lockdown, and then beat the Canadian Blondes, who cash in their rematch four months after losing the belts, at Great Lakes Crisis on 2nd March 2012, and keep the belts against the Second Sons at March Madness on 12th March and May The Force Be With You on 5th May. The Second Sons earn their shot by winning a four-team match at April Showers on 5th April. At High Noon on 5th June 2012 Smith & Singh keep the belts in a three-way against the Second Sons and Ford & Speed, and a week later, at Summer Showdown on 12th June, they lose them to Firebird and Black Eagle, The Dark Raptors, when Firebird pins Singh with the Phoenix Firebird Splash. The Dark Raptors keep them against the West Texas Peacekeepers at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, the XX Factor at Summernova on 5th August and Spectrum Infinity at Iron on 12th August, and lose them at Back To School on 5th September to Team Honor, Jared Johnson and Lassana Makutsi, when Black Eagle taps out to the Carolina Crossface. The diary's own title records list The Dark Raptors as "June 2012 3" and Team Honor as "September 2012 4". The diary's own title records list their reign as "The Canadian Blondes (4) April 2011 11".

name: MAW Traditional Championship
epitaph: MAW's second singles belt, announced by the narrator at All Or Nothing in February 2009 "in honour of the great success stories of the past". Stevie Grayson wins it in the ten-man Mayhem Battle Royal at March Madness, keeps it against Jay Chord at Spring Fever and Curtis Jenkins at Summer Showdown, and loses it to Darryl Devine at Beach Blast; Devine keeps it from Ultimate Phoenix at Iron. Stevie Grayson regains it from Darryl Devine at Where It All Begins Again in October 2009 and loses it to Hugh de Aske at End Of Days in December; de Aske keeps it against Fumihiro Ota, Hugh Lee, "Bulldozer" Brandon Smith (a time-limit draw) and Kirk Jameson until Aaron Andrews wins it at Spring Fever in April 2010, and Andrews keeps it against Antonio at Mother, May I?. Aaron Andrews keeps it against Casey Valentine and Jared Johnson in a triangle match, Firebird and Toxin until Primus Allen beats him at Iron in August 2010; Allen keeps it against Kirk Jameson and Joe Benning and loses it at Where It All Begins Again in October to Jonnie Perez, who keeps it on the November tour shows. The diary's own title records list Allen under August 2010 and Perez under October 2010. Jonnie Perez keeps it on the December and early January tour shows and against Matthew Gauge at End Of Days, until Gauge wins it at The Rip Chord Invitational on 21st January 2011; Gauge, leaving for Japan, loses it to Hugh de Aske in a three-way with Perez at Leap Into The Unknown on 12th February, and de Aske keeps it against Perez, Jean Cattley and "Regular" Joe Benning. The diary's own title records list Gauge under January 2011 with no defence and "Hugh de Aske (2)" under February 2011. Hugh de Aske keeps it against Fumihiro Ota, Providence, Black Eagle and, in a fifteen-minute draw, Jay Chord, until Primus Allen beats him at Summernova on 12th August 2011 with a Sitout Spinebuster; Allen keeps it against Ernest Youngman and, in a three-way, Steve Flash and Erik Strong. The diary's own title records list "Primus Allen (2)" under August 2011. Primus Allen keeps it against Bradford Peverell at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011, Riley McManus at Season's Beatings, Jared Johnson in a fifteen-minute draw at End Of Days, Kid Arachnid on 5th January 2012 and Kirk Jameson at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January, KC Glenn, the Invitational champion, in a time-limit draw at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February 2012, Randy Bumfhole at Third Time's The Charm on 5th March and Lassana Makutsi at March Madness on 12th March, and loses it at April Showers on 5th April to JD Morgan, who pins him in the six-champion Gold Rush match. JD Morgan keeps it against Bradford Peverell and Lord Geoffrey Windameer in a three-way at Mother, May I? on 12th May, and keeps it in the diary's pages from June to September 2012 against Steve Gumble in a draw at High Noon on 5th June, Amazing Fire Fly at Summer Showdown on 12th June, Gumble at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, Donnie J in a thirty-minute draw for the Traditional and All Action titles at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, Black Eagle at Beach Blast on 12th July, Sean Deeley at South East Grand Parade on 9th August and Rudy Velasquez at Iron on 12th August; he is pinned by Deeley in a six-man match at Back To School on 5th September, a non-title match, and is still the champion in the diary's pages for September 2012. The diary's own title records list "JD Morgan April 2012 12 Won in a Gold Rush match".

name: Rip Chord Invitational
epitaph: MAW's annual tournament, whose winner the diary's own title records list under "Rip Chord Invitational" and whose champion the text treats as guaranteed a title shot. Antonio is the 2008 winner; at The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2009 Kid Arachnid beats Fumihiro Ota in the final and is unmasked as Rip Chord's son Jay (the record line reads "Kid Arachnid (Jay Chord)"). Jay Chord, the 2009 winner, cashes in the title shot the Invitational guaranteed him at The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2010, after losing his quarter-final to Erik Strong. Primus Allen beats Strong in the 2010 final with the Running Powerslam and becomes the champion; the diary's own title records list him as "Primus Allen" under January 2010. Primus Allen says at Eleventh Hour in November 2010 that he will not defend the Invitational crown at the 2011 tournament but cash in the guaranteed title shot it carries, a year after his win, against Aaron Andrews. Kirk Jameson wins the 2011 tournament on 21st January 2011 by beating Antonio, Firebird and Hugh de Aske on the one night, after a field that took in qualifiers at Remember November, Season's Beatings, End Of Days and New Year, Old Rivalries and a quarter-final on a tour show; Primus Allen, the holder, has by then spent his crown's title shot on Aaron Andrews. The diary's own title records list Jameson under January 2011. Kirk Jameson spends the guaranteed title shot of his crown on Aaron Andrews at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011 and loses. The 2012 tournament is a field of eight, with qualifiers at Season's Beatings, End Of Days and New Year, Old Rivalries and the rest on 12th January 2012, when Kid Arachnid beats Jared Johnson, Firebird and JD Morgan on the one night and is unmasked as KC Glenn; the diary's own title records list him as "Kid Arachnid (KC Glenn)" under January 2012, and the narrator notes that tew.com now rates the show of Above Average importance, the company's first. In the diary's pages from June to July 2012 KC Glenn, the holder, cashes in a guaranteed title shot against Aaron Andrews at Summer Showdown on 12th June and loses; after Beach Blast on 12th July he leaves MAW.

name: MAW Trios Championship
epitaph: MAW's trios belts, announced by Rip Chord at All Or Nothing in February 2010 after Ultimate Phoenix's lucha experience and his trouble with The Firm. The Watch meet The Firm at March Madness to decide the first champions, and The Firm (Jean Cattley, Darryl Devine and Ryan Powell) win; they keep the belts against the Internet Favourites and Fumihiro Ota at April Showers. The diary's own title records list the first reign as "Cattley, Allen & Powell". The Firm keeps the belts against Shane Nelson, Amazing Fire Fly and Riley McManus at Summer Showdown in June 2010, with Primus Allen standing in for Darryl Devine, and loses them to Fumihiro Ota, Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh at Hotter Than Hot in July; the new champions keep them against Ricochet, Sharp and Toxin at Summernova and against Jared Johnson, Nelson Callum and Roderick Remus at Eleventh Hour in November 2010. The diary's own title records list the two reigns as "Cattley, Allen & Powell March 2010" and "Smith, Ota & Singh July 2010". Fumihiro Ota, Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh lose the belts to The Triple Threat (Jared Johnson, Roderick Remus and Nelson Callum) at Season's Beatings on 12th December 2010, when Firebird distracts Ota; the new champions keep them at End Of Days and on four tour shows. The diary's own title records list the reign as "Johnson, Remus & Callum December 2010 7". The Triple Threat keep the belts on the May and early July tour shows until Kid Arachnid, Chance Fortune and Randy Bumfhole, billed as The Firm, take them at Summernova on 12th August 2011; The Firm keep them against The Fallen at Back To School. The diary's own title records list the new champions as "Arachnid, Fortune & Bumfhole August 2011 1". The Second Sons, Casey Valentine, Cameron Vessey (on loan from USPW) and Antonio, take the belts from The Firm at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011, Valentine pinning Kid Arachnid; at Eleventh Hour on 12th November Rip Chord says he does not like championships that let two men rely on a third and retires the Trios titles, creating the All Action title in their place. The diary's own title records list the last champions as "Vessey, Valentine & Antonio October 2011 - Retired November 2011".

name: MAW All Action Championship
epitaph: MAW's newest belt, announced by Rip Chord at Eleventh Hour on 12th November 2011 as the replacement for the Trios titles he has just retired: held by the man best able to adapt to changing conditions, it is to be defended in randomly selected matches whose stipulation the champion learns only just before the bell. JD Morgan wins it that night in a ten-man battle royal (the diary's own title records say "Won in a Battle Royal") and keeps it against Ernest Youngman in a submission match at Farewell Tour on 22nd November. At Remember November on 26th November the belt is up for grabs all night, a pin or submission anywhere being enough, and it passes through Kid Arachnid, Black Eagle, Wanda Fish (the first woman to hold it), Knuckles and Amazing Fire Fly before JD Morgan wins it back with a chair. He keeps it against Jonnie Perez and Providence at End Of Days and Riley McManus at New Year, Old Rivalries, Bradford Peverell at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February 2012, in a straight wrestling match, Wanda Fish and Fumihiro Ota in a Triple Threat at All Or Nothing on 12th February, Kashmir Singh at Third Time's The Charm on 5th March and Kirk Jameson in a submission match at March Madness on 12th March, and at April Showers on 5th April survives the six-champion Gold Rush match and takes the Traditional title from Primus Allen as well. Donnie J takes the All Action belt from him in a ladder match at South East Crisis on 8th April; Aaron Andrews wins it from Donnie J in a title-versus-title match at May The Force Be With You on 5th May and loses it back to him at Great Lakes Madness on 9th May in a two-out-of-three-falls match, and Donnie J keeps it in the diary's pages from June to August 2012 against Father Johan in a pole match at High Noon on 5th June, Firebird in a submission match at South East Madness on 9th June, Eddie Powell and Citizen X at Summer Showdown on 12th June, Firebird again at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, JD Morgan in a thirty-minute draw for this and the Traditional title at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, Powell and Rudy Velasquez at Summernova on 5th August and Providence in a ladder match at South East Grand Parade on 9th August. At Iron on 12th August Rip Chord says the title can change hands anywhere, and Black Eagle, helped by Firebird, pins Donnie backstage for the belt; Firebird turns on Eagle in a corridor and Donnie, after hitting Firebird with a metal briefcase, pins Eagle to take it back the same night. The diary's own title records list "Black Eagle (2) August 2012 3" and "Donnie J (3) August 2012 0". Donnie J is still the champion in the diary's pages for September 2012. The diary's own title records list "JD Morgan (2) November 2011 7".
